title: Maintaining Proper Pitch in Horizontal Drainage Lines
description: Correct slope is essential for functional gravity-fed drainage systems. A common misconception is assuming that a steeper slope always results in better drainage. If a horizontal drain line is sloped too steeply, liquids flow rapidly while solid waste moves much slower, separating the liquid carrier from the solids. Over time, this separation leaves dry solids stranded inside the pipe, leading to recurring blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope allows waste water to pool. Following standard plumbing code slope guidelines ensures water moves at a self-scouring velocity, keeping solid waste suspended and moving smoothly to the sewer main.

Maintaining Proper Pitch in Horizontal Drainage Lines

Correct slope is essential for functional gravity-fed drainage systems. A common misconception is assuming that a steeper slope always results in better drainage. If a horizontal drain line is sloped too steeply, liquids flow rapidly while solid waste moves much slower, separating the liquid carrier from the solids. Over time, this separation leaves dry solids stranded inside the pipe, leading to recurring blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope allows waste water to pool. Following standard plumbing code slope guidelines ensures water moves at a self-scouring velocity, keeping solid waste suspended and moving smoothly to the sewer main.
